mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during high inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately eroding profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met in at least 70% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 97 for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, reflecting supply-side contraction, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in FEDFUNDS and a decrease in CPIAUCSL by more than 0.2% indicates a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with falling inflation, which historically has been associated with positive equity returns over the next 5 trading days due to rate-cut expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of such co-occurrences.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly rise in HOUST and PAYEMS above 1% indicates strengthening housing demand alongside rising employment, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > +1% AND PAYEMS > +1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in PAYEMS above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a significant labor market weakening, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 2% for six consecutive months signals robust retail sales growth, which typically precedes positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate revenue outlook.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered periods.
